American colonists and Americans in the new republic experienced one constant: change. From changing political identities, geographic boundaries, and conceptions of freedom, American lives constantly evolved. This seminar will explore the ways that craftspeople and cabinetmakers navigated this ever-shifting political and social landscape and the ways that they reflected shifting American and European tastes and identities in their work.

You can join us in Winston-Salem or online for this two day seminar. Participants will engage in two days of lectures, including a keynote address by Dr. Tiffany Momon, Director of the Center for Historic Preservation, Middle Tennessee State University and Founder of the Black Craftspeople Digital Archive, as well as opportunities to participate in pre-conference workshops and a furniture open house in MESDA’s study galleries.

Learn how southern women exercised power in the early American South.

At 2:00 PM, join us to learn about the Edenton Tea Party, one of the first organized women’s political protests in America. On October 25, 1774, a group of Edenton women led by Penelope (Padgett) Barker (1728-1796) pledged to boycott imported British tea and cloth in response to the Tea Act of 1774. News of their “tea party” reached London, where it was reported in the Morning Chronicle and London Advertiser on January 16, 1775.
These guided tours are included with your standard admission.

This two-hour walk will begin at the Over-the-Rhine Museum at 3 West McMicken Avenue to briefly discuss the exhibition, Second Look: Danny Ransohoff’s Cityscapes Through New Eyes. From there, with copies of Danny Ransohoff’s historic photos in hand, the group will walk to five of the locations featured in the show. Once oriented in each spot, we will discuss change over time by comparing the photograph of the past and present before our eyes. We may even begin to imagine the neighborhood’s future. This walk will be led by University of Cincinnati Research Assistant Professor of History, Anne Delano Steinert.

Additional Information: Participants should come dressed for the weather and expect moderate exercise. Please RSVP to hello@otrmuseum.org to stay informed in case of inclement weather.

Spotlight Weekends highlight FotoFocus Biennial Venues within specific geographic locations where artists and curators will be on site for talks, tours, special events, and featured programming. This is an opportunity to immerse yourself in the vibrant energy of the FotoFocus Biennial, exploring art within the communities that create and present it.
The Bus Tour is now full. To join the waitlist, please email pass@fotofocus.org.
8:00am Meet at FotoFocus Center / Ziegler Garage
8:30am Depart Cincinnati
10:00am Wright State University
Elizabeth Mead: Incident(als): objects + things, sculpture + photographs. Sculptural objects and images paired together to magnify the significance of seemingly small things and fleeting experiences.
Holly Roberts: Confluence. Hauntingly layered visual narratives experimenting with hybridity and transformation, where image and imagination converge.
Tours given by professors and curators Stefan Chinov and Tracy Longley-Cook.
11:00am Sinclair Community College Art Galleries
Katria Foster: Domestic Affair. Highlights physical and mental aspects of the female perspective, ruminating on themes of control, manipulation, and unquestioned social constructs.
Emily Wiethorn: The Death of You and Me. Photographic series examining memory, suffering, and the life-altering effects of trauma.
Introduction with Galleries Coordinator, Amanda Darrah, followed by self-guided tour.
11:35pm Dayton Society of Artists
Luminous Flow. An open call positing long-exposure photography as a way to reveal motion, energy, and the passage of time through landscapes, cityscapes, and experimental processes.
Short presentation of the exhibition provided by juror Gregory Changa Freeman.
Stivers School for the Arts

Heather Wetzel: Considering the Cultivated. Interrogates the role humans have on the environment, ecosystems, and food production through historic photographic processes, paper making, book arts, and sculptural materials.
Gallery tour led by Leah Stahl, Director of Photography and Media Arts.
12:20pm Edward A. Dixon Gallery
Picturing Tomorrow: Speculative Futures in Lens-Based Art. Invites artists to consider how photography can be used to document not just what is, but also speculate on what could be.
Gallery tour led by owner and founder, Ed Dixon.
12:50pm Lunch
1:20pm Dayton Art Institute

Looking for Japan: Early Japanese Photography. Captures Japan’s Meiji period through postcards, albums, albumen travel photographs, and hanging scroll collotypes, reflecting on social transformation and Western influences.
Getting Technical: Alternative Photographic Processes. A group exhibition spanning 175 years, embracing photography’s founding spirit of experimentation through uncommon techniques and adaptations.
Curator talk with Mariah Postlewait, Sara M. and Michelle Vance Waddell Curator of Feminist Art and Photography.
2:00pm The Contemporary Dayton
Ella Kraimer: Appearances. Large-scale photographic self-portraits examining identity, performance, and consumption in a digital culture shaped by spectacle and self-surveillance.
Stacy Kranitz: Ain’t No Grave Gonna Hold My Body Down. Documents how images and archives have shaped and distorted public understanding of Appalachia across generations.

Public artist talk featuring Stacy Kranitz in conversation with Andrew Milward, author and Director of Graduate Studies, Creative Writing Division, at the University of Kentucky. Interim Director and Chief Curator Heather Jones will also be on site.
3:45pm University of Dayton: Roger Glass Center for the Arts
Darshan. Collaborative documentary work of India exploring the Hindu philosophy and phenomenon of darshan (“to see”).
Gallery talk led by Nicholaus Arnold, Galleries Director.
5:00pm Rosewood Arts Center
Amanda Bradley: Notations from Home. Images exploring diasporic notions of home across geographies and time, using the camera as a tool for note-taking and relationship building.
Trent Davis Bailey: The North Fork. Childhood memories intertwined with images and moments from family farms on Colorado’s Western Slope.

Gallery tour and artist talk led by Trent Davis Bailey. Laura Truitt, Gallery Coordinator, and Shayna McConville, Division Manager of Cultural Arts, will also be on site. Reception with light refreshments to follow.
7:15pm Arrive in Cincinnati

11:30am Wexner Center for the Arts

Sammy Baloji: When Extraction Becomes Form It Speaks In Borrowed Tongues. Uncovers how colonial extraction shaped the flow of people, materials, forms, and culture across Africa, Europe, and the Atlantic world through photography, film, and sculpture.

Gallery tour led by Sarah Robison, Curator of Teaching, Learning, and Interpretation, and Rebecca Lowery, Curator of Exhibitions. Interim Executive Director & Head of Advancement hope to join as well.

1:30pm Columbus Museum of Art

Queer Constellations: Photographs from the Aronowitz Family Collection. Traces artistic lineage and identity through photographs by and about queer artists, illustrating how photographers across generations shape histories and create visibility.
Gallery tour led by Kaitlin Booher, Associate Curator of Photography.
2:30pm Columbus College of Art & Design: Beeler Gallery
Haunting. Examines time as a haunting force, reaching across burial grounds, pandemics, atomic history, gun violence, and ecological loss to reveal what the visible image cannot hold.
Gallery tour led by new Executive Director Kyle Herrington and Registrar Melissa Vogley.
3:15pm Shot Tower Gallery

One Shot. Alumni exhibition highlighting the impact of the Photography Career Program at Fort Hayes, an incubator for emerging image-makers to explore photography as a form of artistic expression and storytelling.
Gallery tour led by Stephen Takacs, Career-Technical Education (CTE) Photography Instructor.
4:00pm ROY G BIV Gallery

Franklinton Across Time: The Floodplain Imagination. A living archive examining the history of one of Columbus’ oldest neighborhoods through contemporary lens-based work, archival materials, interviews, and site-responsive installations, reflecting on collective memory and urban change.
Gallery tour with Executive Gallery Director, Bethani Blake.
Reception & light bites.

Spotlight Weekends highlight FotoFocus Biennial Venues within specific geographic locations where artists and curators will be on site for talks, tours, special events, and featured programming. This is an opportunity to immerse yourself in the vibrant energy of the FotoFocus Biennial, exploring art within the communities that create and present it.
The Bus Tour is now full. To join the waitlist, please email pass@fotofocus.org.
8:30am Meet at FotoFocus Center / Ziegler Garage
9:00am Kennedy Heights Arts Center
Cultural Ties. Celebrates Latin American culture through photography, mixed media, and short films, offering a multi-sensory exploration of place, history, and identity.
Gallery tour led by Mallory Feltz, Director of Exhibitions and Public Art. Artists and film curator Mary Leonard will be in attendance and will discuss their work.
10:00am Eisele Gallery
Waiting to Be Seen. A selection of street photography and photojournalism paying tribute to the diversity of urban life and to the lens-based artists who witness and capture it.
Gallery tour led by Sandy Eichert, curator, and/or David Smith, gallery owner.
10:45am Cincinnati Art Club

Contemporary Tintype Portraits and Altered Historic Images. Tintype portraits by Ricky Willis Tintypes and Blue Creek Tinworks celebrating the local photographic community alongside altered historic images from the Cincinnati Art Club archives.
Curatorial overview provided by Kip Eagen. Artists/studios may also be present to speak about the process and history of tintype photography.
11:30am Lunch @ Swell Art Cafe
12:15pm Wave Pool
Forgetting is Everywhere. Work by four artists exploring transformations both slow and sudden, unexpected but also predestined. Presented in conjunction with Swell.
Gallery tour led by curator Calcagno Cullen.
1:00pm Studio Kroner
Erika NJ Allen: Beneath All Distance. Investigates deep time, material memory, and humanity’s relationship to landscapes shaped by endurance and change through analog photography and ceramics.
Open gallery roaming and artist talk with Erika NJ Allen. Paul Kroner will also be on site.
1:45pm Art Academy of Cincinnati
Depth of Field. An open call highlighting student artists considering the present state of photography and its possible future directions.
Noel Bassam Mohammad Maghathe: Over Everything. Examines how memory is shaped, altered, and reconstructed through the act of retrieval, initiating a dialogue between longing, connection, and memory.
Untwined/Interwoven. Reflects on concepts of place and time, examining the ephemeral, impermanent, and fragmented nature of photography.

Accra Shepp: Bearing Witness. Presents three bodies of work—Occupying Wall Street, The Covid Journals, and The Islands of New York—that delve into subjects often overlooked or intentionally misconstrued.
Gallery talks led by Michael Hurst, Director of Exhibitions; Rachel Reisert, Head of Photography; and student curators.
3:00pm Taft Museum of Art

Edie McKee Harper: Modernist at Play. Over 100 works across a variety of media, including photography, demonstrate the artist’s distinctive modernist vision, highlighting her minimalist and often playful style.
Introduction by Curator Tamera Lenz Muente followed by a self-guided tour.
3:45pm Annex Gallery

Juan-Sí González: I.T.I.N.E.R.A.T.I.O.N.S. Explores the boundary between documentary and fiction, reinterpreting reality as metaphor and calling attention to shared physical, ideological, and psychological landscapes.
Artist talk with Juan-Sí González. Jorge Rodríguez Diez, Executive Director and Chief Curator, and Jens Rosenkrantz may also be on site.

4:15pm Depart Annex Gallery. Bus returns to Ziegler Garage on Sycamore Street.

It’s the unofficial kickoff to the holiday season in Cleveland! Join the tradition at Christmas Ale First Pour®. The first taste of the holiday seasonal classic taps exclusively at the GLBC brewpub on Thursday, October 15, 2026.

Brewpub doors will open promptly at 11AM, with the first fresh keg of Christmas Ale tapped at 11:30AM after a special toast to the season. Read on to learn about our full seasonal lineup, find out how you can celebrate First Pour at Home, and enter for a chance to win a VIP Christmas Ale First Pour experience!

Remember your ID! All guests must be 21 or older with a valid ID to purchase or consume alcohol. No ID, no alcohol. No exceptions. Reservations will not be accepted for First Pour, and tables will be available on a first-come, first served basis, with a three-hour limit. While supplies last.
2026 CHRISTMAS ALE FIRST POUR HIGHLIGHTS:
<ul>
• Cleveland Carolers (10AM)
• Christmas Ale ceremonial keg delivery (11AM)
• The First Pour of Christmas Ale (11:30AM)
• Christmas Ale food specials (all day)
• Brewnuts holiday donuts available (11:30AM, while supplies last)
• Be the first to shop 2026 holiday merch
• Photo opps
Entertainment:
<ul>
• 11AM – 1:30PM: Cats on Holiday
• 2PM – 5PM: DJ Red-I
• 6PM – 9PM: Apostle Jones
FIRST POUR WINTER CLOTHING DRIVE:
Help us fill the bus for Sub Zero Mission, an organization providing critical cold-weather and outreach supplies to those in need.
Sub Zero’s greatest needs are new or gently used:
<ul>
• Adult men’s winter boots
• Adult men’s winter coats sized XL-5XL
• Tents
• Sleeping bags

They are also accepting adult men’s winter hats (not homemade), winter gloves, and new socks. Not attending but want to help make an impact? Shop the Sub Zero Mission wish list and donate online here.
GIFT SHOP HIGHLIGHTS:

Great Lakes holiday merch hits our gift shop first on First Pour Day so you can get a head start on your holiday gifting. Be the first to shop 2026 Great Lakes holiday merch, including collaborations with Homage and Emily Roggenburk!
Note: Christmas Ale will NOT be available for purchase in the gift shop during First Pour. See complete Christmas Ale release details below.
FIRST POUR AT HOME PACKAGES:

A limited number of Christmas Ale 1/6 bbl kegs will be available for purchase in our gift shop so you can host your own First Pour at home! You MUST make a reservation at the this link no later than October 10 to purchase a Christmas Ale keg. All reserved kegs must be picked up in person at the GLBC gift shop during your selected time slot on Thursday, October 15th. Unclaimed kegs will be made available for purchase to the public if not picked up within their time slot. Payment and valid photo ID are required at time of pick-up. All reservations must be made via the link. We are unable to accept orders over the phone or hold kegs. Keg pricing for a 1/6 bbl of Christmas Ale is $115 plus tax and $30 deposit (refundable). Keg pricing for a 1/6 bbl of Barrel Aged Christmas Ale is $195 plus tax and $30 deposit (refundable). Reserve your Christmas Ale keg here.
WIN THE ULTIMATE FIRST POUR VIP EXPERIENCE:

Want to make your 2026 First Pour celebration extra special for yourself and your right-hand elf? Tell us who you’d share the First Pour with and why for a chance to win a First Pour VIP Experience including a private brewery tour, lunch for two, a “sleigh” full of GLBC holiday goodies, and VIP behind-the-bar access to the first taste of the season. Enter for a chance to win here.
OFFICIAL FIRST POUR PARTIES:

Can’t make it to Cleveland for the fun? We’re celebrating Christmas Ale First Pour in cities all over! Stay tuned to greatlakesbrewing.com/merrychristmasale for up-to-date listings of First Pour events near you, which will be added in the coming weeks and updated throughout the season.
CHRISTMAS ALE RELEASE DETAILS:
October 15: Christmas Ale draft-only release exclusively at the GLBC brewpub! Sorry, no growler or crowler fills on First Pour day. No reservations.

October 16: The first cans, bottles, and kegs of Christmas Ale will be available for purchase exclusively at the GLBC gift shop. Sorry, we are unable to hold or reserve any beer. Gift shop opens at 10AM.
October 19: Cans, bottles, and kegs of Christmas Ale will begin appearing throughout all GLBC markets.
MORE UPCOMING HOLIDAY EVENTS:

First Pour is just the beginning! Stay tuned for fun seasonal events including our already announced Christmas Ale VIP Brewery Experience Tours taking place select dates in October, November, andDecember.
NEW HOLIDAY PARTY PACK:

The Holiday Party Pack joins our seasonal lineup with a mix of four festive brews in a holiday party-themed package, perfect for celebrations. The Holiday Party Pack releases October 19 and includes three (3) cans of each:
<ul>
• Christmas Ale: the holiday classic, brewed with ginger, cinnamon, and honey; 7.5% ABV
• Cran Orange Wheat: a Wheat Ale brewed with a medley of cranberry and orange; 5.5% ABV (also available in 6-packs)
• Cookie Exchange Milk Stout: a rotating Milk Stout now exclusive to the Holiday Party Pack, with a Snickerdoodle-inspired flavor for 2026; 5.5% ABV
• Snowscape Winter Lager: a NEW richly layered yet balanced Winter Lager; 6.0% ABV
NEW SNOWSCAPE WINTER LAGER:

In addition to its inclusion in the Holiday Party Pack, Snowscape Winter Lager releases in draft, can 12-packs, and bottle 6-packs. The slightly dark 6.0% ABV lager brings smooth and layered flavors and a cozy lodge-inspired package to our winter lineup and lager legacy.
BARREL AGED CHRISTMAS ALE:

Barrel Aged Christmas Ale returns for a limited time in 16 oz. Can 4-Packs to make the season even brighter! Find it in the GLBC gift shop on Friday, October 16, and throughout our distribution footprint starting Monday, October 19.
MORE BARREL AGED TREATS COMING SOON:

Barrel Aged Blackout Stout returns in November for a limited time in 16 oz. can 4-packs. New this year, a Caramel Pecan variant of the beloved Imperial Stout also makes its way to our markets in 16 oz. can 4-packs alongside our classic legacy barrel aged offering for more holiday sipping and gifting. Caramel Pecan Blackout Stout balances rich caramel depth and toasted pecan character.

Want to dive even deeper into the wonderful world of brewing at Ohio’s original craft brewery? Are you a super fan of Christmas Ale? Celebrate the holiday season with us on these special Holiday VIP Experience tours, where you’ll go beyond the beer with a Brewery Exclusive Experience. Nerd out with behind-the-scenes access to our sensory lab and taste limited and small-batch brews and variations of our classic Christmas Ale you won’t find anywhere else—just like the pros do!

Guests will grab their first taste of our carefully crafted beer in our Beer Symposium before venturing into the production facility for an up-close look at our brewing, cellaring, and packaging processes. Get a personal tour of our sensory lab with our Sensory Specialist and Advanced Cicerone®, and put your tastebuds to the test with samples of Christmas Ale you won’t find anywhere else! Join us for The Last Voyage: Remembering the Edmund Fitzgerald, a presentation honoring the crew of the Edmund Fitzgerald and remembering the ship’s final voyage.

The evening’s talk will highlight the building and career of the iconic freighter, its impact on Great Lakes cities like Cleveland, the events of its last voyage, and explore the lasting legacy of its sinking in the Great Lakes region.
The presentation will take place November 9, 10, and 11. Seating opens at 5:30 PM, with the presentation beginning at 6 PM and concluding at 7:14 PM, followed by a moment of silence.

During the event, $1 from every pint of Edmund Fitzgerald Porter sold will be donated to the Great Lakes Shipwreck Museum.

Join us for The Last Voyage: Remembering the Edmund Fitzgerald, a presentation honoring the crew of the Edmund Fitzgerald and remembering the ship’s final voyage.

The evening’s talk will highlight the building and career of the iconic freighter, its impact on Great Lakes cities like Cleveland, the events of its last voyage, and explore the lasting legacy of its sinking in the Great Lakes region.
The presentation will take place November 9, 10, and 11. Seating opens at 5:30 PM, with the presentation beginning at 6 PM and concluding at 7:14 PM, followed by a moment of silence.

During the event, $1 from every pint of Edmund Fitzgerald Porter sold will be donated to the Great Lakes Shipwreck Museum.

Want to dive even deeper into the wonderful world of brewing at Ohio’s original craft brewery? Are you a super fan of Christmas Ale? Celebrate the holiday season with us on these special Holiday VIP Experience tours, where you’ll go beyond the beer with a Brewery Exclusive Experience. Nerd out with behind-the-scenes access to our sensory lab and taste limited and small-batch brews and variations of our classic Christmas Ale you won’t find anywhere else—just like the pros do!

Guests will grab their first taste of our carefully crafted beer in our Beer Symposium before venturing into the production facility for an up-close look at our brewing, cellaring, and packaging processes. Then it really gets good. Get a personal tour of our sensory lab with our Sensory Specialist and Advanced Cicerone®, and put your tastebuds to the test with samples of Christmas Ale you won’t find anywhere else! Tours last approximately 90 minutes and include a tasting of up to six Christmas Ale variations in the Sensory lab, three beer tokens for samples of your choice in our Beer Symposium, and a souvenir glass to take home!
THE FINE PRINT

Choose your tour date and time carefully! Payment is non-refundable, and event date and time is non-transferable. Our tours start promptly at their scheduled time; no exceptions. Guests arriving late are not guaranteed a chance to join their tour. Please allow time to find parking and arrive at least 10 minutes before your scheduled tour start time.

Please be aware that buying out all of the tickets for a brewery tour does not guarantee it will be a private event for you and your guests. A limited amount of walk-up tickets are available on a first come, first served basis at the start of every public tour day. Please visit the Beer Symposium to inquire about any open availability. If you are interested in a private tour, please contact us directly at 216.325.7846 for additional details.

Don’t forget your ID! Guests must be 21 or older with a valid ID to consume or purchase alcohol. Guests without a valid ID at check-in will not receive beer samples. No guest under 21 will be permitted to consume alcohol; no exceptions. This tour is for guests 21+ only.

Visitors planning to visit the brewery MUST wear closed-toe shoes (i.e. boots or sneakers; no flip flops or sandals.) This is for your personal safety and the safety of our guests. Our brewery is housed in a 19th century building with narrow spaces and multiple stairwells. Be aware that breweries are hot and loud, especially in packaging areas and during the summer months.

Tour availability is subject to change. Details and offerings subject to change without notice. Questions? Contact us at 216.771.4404 or glbcinfo@greatlakesbrewing.com.
